newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt reviewing capital market legislation.
newsitem.headline: Egypt reviewing capital market legislation.

text.p: The Egyptian government is reviewing the law governing the stock exchange, Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi said in remarks published on Saturday.

The current law on capital markets, passed only in 1992, is widely seen as needing amendment to cope with the sudden expansion and growing sophistication of the stock exchange and capital market activity.

Tatawi, quoted in the government newspaper al-Ahram, said proposed new legislation included clear rules for a central share depositary, the functions of market makers, regulations on the use of information and rules to prevent price manipulation.
The minister also said that the authorities were thinking of lifting the 49 percent limit on the stake foreign interests can hold in Egyptian-based insurance companies.
She said that public-sector banks and insurance companies sold assets worth 1.65 billion pounds ($490 million) in joint-venture companies last year.
The sale of these assets was part of the privatisation process but separate from mainstream privatisation, which raised about 2.3 billion pounds for the state in 1996.
The government intends to continue selling off the state's stake in joint-venture companies throughout this year.
The public-sector banks and insurance companies still hold assets worth 1.55 billion pounds in joint-venture companies, Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily said this week.

But the banks are in effect reinvesting some of the proceeds from sales in new projects. Tatawi told al-Ahram they were taking stakes of between five and 25 percent in 42 new projects with a total capitalisation of six billion pounds.
